sovereign_country.strategic_role: 拉美美元金融中枢、私人利益基金会（PIF）与运河船舶登记

business_scope.primary_industry_name: GPS-Sealed Bonded Road Feeder Service for International Airports

meta_jurisdiction_context.jurisdiction_name_en: Republic of Panama (Unitary National Jurisdiction; no sub-state tax distinction)
meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Civil Law (codified Spanish heritage) with Hybrid commercial adaptations, including private interest foundations and Anglo-American influenced corporate, fiduciary, and maritime practice
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: United States-Panama Trade Promotion Agreement (in force 31 October 2012)
European Union-Central America Association Agreement (provisional application from 2013, includes investment and trade disciplines for Panama)
Panama-Netherlands Agreement for the Exchange of Information on Tax Matters and related Tax Treaty framework (2000)
Panama-Spain Treaty for the Reciprocal Protection and Promotion of Investments (1997)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Law 23 of 27 April 2015 (AML/CFT framework for Financial and Non-Financial Regulated Sectors) as amended by Law 52 of 2016, Law 70 of 2019, and related implementing Executory Decrees; Law 25 of 12 June 1995 ('Ley de Fundaciones de Interés Privado') and Executive Decree 915 of 2004 (Foundation Charter regulation); Law 129 of 17 August 2020, as amended by Law 254 of 2021, and Executive Decree 54 of 2021 (National Beneficial Ownership Registry 'Registro de Beneficiarios Finales' administered by the Dirección General de Ingresos); Law 32 of 1927 (Codificación Comercial, corporations); Resolution No. 201-2010 and UAF directives on CDD and PEP risk. Sub-sector risk rating: 'Low_Risk_Standard' for the PIF holding structure, with enhanced attention to the customs bonded truck fleet licensee, which is subject to Aduanas (ANA) transport licensing and ATT route regulation.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified copy of the civil passport of each natural-person founder, council member, and protector
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent civil registry or passport authority of the founder's country of nationality
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille where the issuing state is a 1961 Apostille Convention member; otherwise full consular legalization at the Panamanian Embassy/Consulate

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Incorporation, Certificate of Good Standing, and board resolution appointing the proposed foundation officers, where a founder is a body corporate
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Companies registry and corporate secretary/board of the jurisdiction of the corporate founder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or consular legalization of the jurisdiction of origin

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified copy of the registry of directors and shareholders, or equivalent beneficial ownership certificate, of any corporate founder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Corporate registry or licensed corporate service provider of the founder entity's jurisdiction
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or consular legalization of the jurisdiction of origin

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized and apostilled power of attorney in favor of the Panama resident agent/attorney for submission and signature of the foundation charter
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Public notary of the jurisdiction of grantor plus Apostille-issuing authority (or Panamanian consulate for non-Hague states)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank and professional reference letter (AML/KYC due diligence) confirming source of funds of the initial foundation endowment
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Regulated financial institution or licensed lawyer/accountant of the founder's jurisdiction
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarization plus Hague Apostille or consular legalization, unless waived under the resident agent's KYC policy

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all founders, foundation council members, protectors, contingent beneficiaries, and ultimate beneficial owners against the United Nations Security Council Consolidated List, OFAC SDN List, European Union consolidated financial sanctions list, FATF public statements including jurisdictions under enhanced monitoring, and Panamanian national lists maintained by the Unidad de Análisis Financiero (UAF) and the Dirección General de Ingresos. PEP designation requires enhanced due diligence, written senior-manager approval within the Panamanian resident agent, and mandatory disclosure of source of wealth and source of funds. Cash contributions above USD 10,000 or in any amount inconsistent with the declared business profile are prohibited under the PIF's internal AML policy. The resident agent must file Suspicious Transaction Reports (STR) with the UAF where required by Law 23 of 2015.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Registro Público de Panamá - Mercantile Section (online name reservation and inquiry via the Registro Público de Panamá electronic services portal; https://www.registro-publico.gob.pa)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The foundation charter and the name must be registered in the Latin script; the statute is drafted principally in Spanish, but a registered name may be in a foreign language using Latin characters. Any non-Latin script name of the founder or of the foundation must be transliterated phonetically into Latin characters; the transliteration must be consistent across the charter, the resident agent's records, and the DGI UBO filing. The name must include the word 'Fundación' or 'Foundation' as appropriate and must not be identical or deceptively similar to a name already recorded in the Public Registry.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: If the name is rejected, the applicant or its resident agent files a written reconsideration petition ('recurso de reconsideración') with the Registrar of the Mercantile Section within 5 working days of the refusal notice, proposing either a clarifying argument or a revised name. If denied, an administrative appeal ('recurso de apelación') may be lodged with the Director General of the Public Registry within 5 working days of the reconsideration rejection. Exhaustion of administrative remedies permits judicial challenge before the Third Chamber of the Supreme Court of Justice ('Sala Tercera de lo Contencioso Administrativo') within the applicable statutory period. Where the rejection is based solely on confusing similarity, the safer commercial practice is to file a new name reservation immediately and, if required, obtain written consent from the prior registrant through a notarized letter of no objection.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Permissible only for the PIF holding layer, which may maintain its registered office at the licensed resident agent's address in Panama City. A virtual office without any physical infrastructure is not acceptable for the underlying customs bonded truck fleet licensee; the operating entity (whether the PIF or a subsidiary SPV) must evidence a physical operational address, secured fleet parking, GPS-sealed tracking systems, customs registration under Autoridad Nacional de Aduanas, and a land transport operating license issued by the Autoridad de Tránsito y Transporte Terrestre. Accordingly, the formation stage accepts virtual office for the PIF, but the business plan must reflect physical substance for the operating license.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: PIF holding layer: 10% probability of unannounced inspection in the first three years. Underlying customs bonded truck operator: 55% probability of physical inspection by ANA/ATT within the first three operating years, including fleet-level GPS seal verification, customs warehouse and parking facility inspection, and payroll/subcontractor documentation review.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Public Registry name availability search and reservation fee
Notarization, Hague Apostille, or consular legalization of founder documents, powers of attorney, and corporate extracts
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Competent notary, Apostille-issuing authority, or Panamanian consulate of the jurisdiction of origin
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market notarial and consular fee, approximately USD 50-150 per document

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Drafting and execution of the Private Interest Foundation charter and internal regulations
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Panama licensed attorney / law firm acting as resident agent
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market fixed fee for PIF formation, including constitutional document, council appointment, and protector provisions

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Public Registry inscription fee for the foundation charter
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory registry tariff for inscription of the act of foundation

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Resident agent and registered office service - first year annual retainer
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market annual corporate service fee

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: AML/KYC onboarding, PEP/sanctions screening, and DGI Beneficial Ownership Registry (RBF) filing
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Law firm compliance department; Dirección General de Ingresos (for any RBF registration fee)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Fixed compliance fee plus official RBF filing tariff, if applicable

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Ley 25 de 12 de julio de 1995 (Private Interest Foundations); Articles 1-15, 16-29 and 30-48; as supplemented by the general provisions of Ley 32 de 1927 and Ley 5 de 1998 on registered agents
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registro Público de Panamá - Section of Private Interest Foundations
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Foundation Charter (Escritura Constitutiva / Acta Constitutiva de Fundación de Interés Privado)
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital under Law 25 of 1995. The founder must allocate a reasonable initial patrimony consisting of movable or immovable assets, rights, or a cash endowment. A mandatory escrow bank account is not required, but the registered agent must accept the appointed office and the foundation council must formally receive the initial assets.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED: (1) That the founder subscribes to an initial endowment of USD 10,000 (or equivalent assets) as the foundation's patrimony. (2) That the registered office of the Foundation is fixed at the office of the licensed Registered Agent in Panama City. (3) That the following persons are hereby appointed as members of the Foundation Council for the initial term: [Name] as President, [Name] as Secretary and [Name] as Treasurer. (4) That the Foundation Council is authorised to open bank accounts, lease warehouse space and execute all contracts for customs-bonded road feeder services. (5) That the Registered Agent is authorised to file all statutory corporate registrations.

step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft the Foundation Charter in Spanish, specifying the foundation's purpose (including bonded trucking and airport feeder services, ISIC 5222), registered agent, Foundation Council, asset endowment and dissolution procedures. Submit the draft with identification to a licensed notary and execute the charter before the notary. The notary will authenticate the signatures and prepare the public instrument for registry submission.
required_dossiers: Passport copies of founder and Council members
Certified Spanish translation of foreign passports (if applicable)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary notes defects in the charter or missing information, correct the instrument within two business days and re-notarize the corrected version prior to registry presentation.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Submit the Foundation Charter to the Public Registry
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registro Público de Panamá - Section of Private Interest Foundations
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the notarized Foundation Charter with the Public Registry, along with the official fee payment and the registered agent's acceptance. The registry reviews the instrument for compliance with Law 25 of 1995, including the minimum content, and issues the Foundation's certificate of registration (Firma de Registro).
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registry files an objection or query, address the written observation within 10 business days, amend the affected clause with the notary, and re-submit. A second rejection can be cured by judicial resolution before the Civil Circuit Court.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Obtain the Foundation Certificate and Legal Status Resolution
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registro Público de Panamá - Legalization and Certification Office
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After registration, request the formal certificate of legal existence and the public registry number. Verify that the foundation's full name, registered office, and Foundation Council are correctly recorded. Obtain additional certified copies of the charter for banking and licensing purposes.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Apply for rectification of any typographical discrepancy by presenting the original notarized charter and supporting documentation; the registry will issue a correction order.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Register with the Tax Authority and Obtain the Panama Tax ID (RUC)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI) - Ministry of Economy and Finance
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the tax registration form for the Private Interest Foundation, including the registry certificate, registered agent details, and the Foundation's address. Upon approval, the DGI assigns a permanent NIT/RUC (Registro Único de Contribuyente). This RUC is required for all customs, labor, commercial, and environmental interactions.
required_dossiers: Foundation certificate from the Public Registry
Passports of Council members (copies authenticated by registered agent)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registration application is rejected due to missing data, complete the deficiency notice and resubmit within 5 business days; an administrative appeal lies with the Economic-Financial Appeal Tribunal.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Open the Corporate Bank Account and Deposit Initial Foundation Assets
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Licensed Panamanian Bank designated by the Foundation
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Present the Foundation's registry certificate, the RUC, a certified copy of the charter, and a resolution of the Foundation Council approving the account opening. Complete Customer Due Diligence for the Foundation, Council members, and the beneficial owner. Deposit the initial endowment (US$10,000 or equivalent) and obtain the account confirmation. The bank will issue a compliance acceptance for AML monitoring.
required_dossiers: Tax compliance status certificate (Paz y Salvo)
Bank-specific KYC, reference and financial source forms
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank requests further information under Panama's AML Law 23 of 2015, provide the additional KYC documents within 5 business days. A formal account refusal may be cured by selecting another licensed bank with documentation assistance.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Autoridad de Tránsito y Transporte Terrestre (ATTT) together with Dirección Nacional de Aduanas (ANA) for customs-related bonded operations; commercial license from the Mayor's Office of the Jurisdiction (e.g., Alcaldía de Panamá) under MICI technical supervision
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Licencia de Operación para Transporte de Carga por Carretera con Régimen de Depósito Aduanero (Bonded Truck Fleet Operating License) and Carta de Elegibilidad de Transportista de Carga Bajo Regimen Aduanero

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Category I - Registration (Registro de la Actividad) for low-impact road freight operations; no full EIA required unless the fleet includes a fuel depot or vehicle washing discharge station
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Vehicle diesel exhaust emissions must meet the limits set under Gaceta Oficial No. 29325 (vehicle pollution regulation) and current EU/EPA equivalent emissions for heavy trucks used as airport feeders. Wastewater from any washing bay must have pH 6-9, total suspended solids < 50 mg/L, and hydrocarbons < 10 ppm. Waste tires and WVO-resistant containers must be disposed through MiAMBIENTE-authorized licensed operators.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety inspection and certificate from the Benemérito Cuerpo de Bomberos de Panamá; structural and load-bearing inspection for the vehicle maintenance facility by the Ministry of Housing and Territorial Planning (MIVIOT); workplace hygiene and occupational health clearance under the Ministry of Labor (MITRADEL); and dock/ramp permits from the Civil Aviation Authority if the trucking service operates from an airport Zone of Commercial Operation.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI) of the Ministry of Economy and Finance (MEF); online portal: Sede Electrónica DGI (https://dgi.mef.gob.pa)
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Foreign entities obtain a Panamanian RUC (Registro Único de Contribuyente) by filing the entity registration application with the DGI via the Sede Electrónica portal or through a licensed public accountant/attorney. The foreign entity must submit the authenticated foundation deed, the currently valid registered agent resignation/acceptance letter, proof of appointment of a local fiscal resident representative, and the completed taxpayer application form (Aviso de Inscripción). Upon approval, the DGI issues the RUC and activates the e-Tax 2.0 profile for filing and compliance.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Territorial_Scope (Panamanian Private Interest Foundations are separate taxable persons; only Panama-source income is subject to income tax. Foreign-source income, capital gains, and dividends are generally outside the Panamanian territorial tax net unless repatriated through Panamanian banking channels or connected to a permanent establishment in Panama).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No check-the-box or hybrid-mismatch election exists under Panamanian law. A foundation voluntarily carrying on taxable business in Panama may elect between the ordinary ITBMS scheme or the simplified small-taxpayer regime (for operators under the B/.200,000 annual turnover threshold), and such election is irrevocable for a minimum period under DGI regulations.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: ITBMS (Impuesto de Transferencia de Bienes Corporales Muebles y Servicios) – a territorial VAT-type tax administered by the DGI
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: B/.0 – registration for ITBMS is mandatory for any person or entity performing taxable transfers of goods or services in Panama or in the other taxable Panamanian territory. Small taxpayers with annual gross receipts up to B/.200,000 may register under the simplified ITBMS regime, which substitutes a reduced composite rate for full credit/refund mechanics.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Panama mandates phased electronic invoicing for all ordinary ITBMS taxpayers. Invoices must be generated through DGI-approved software or the DGI web portal, carry a digital signature and a QR code, and be transmitted in real time (API/XML exchange) to the DGI for fiscal validation and stamping. Final acceptance is recorded electronically before the invoice is issued to the client; invoices not cleared through the DGI fiscal repository are null for tax deduction and credit purposes.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero-rating under ITBMS applies to (i) goods physically exported from Panama to a foreign destination, and (ii) services rendered to non-residents, consumed entirely abroad, or directly performed on goods destined for export. The bonded truck fleet feeder service for international air cargo qualifies when the services are covered by a customs transit regime, the transport begins in Panama and ends abroad, and title and risk in the goods transfer to a foreign consignee. The exporter must be an ordinary ITBMS taxpayer and must issue an e-invoice with the zero-rated indicator, retaining all required transport and customs documents.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (Declaración Única de Exportación/DUI)
Bill of Lading / Air Waybill / Master Road Manifest (CMR for bonded truck transit)
Commercial invoice and underlying purchase/sales contract
Inward Remittance Certificate (bank SWIFT MT103 or letter of credit) evidencing receipt of payment from the foreign buyer
Customs custody/bonded transit documentation (T-document or similar transit regime) proving movement from entry point to exit point
GPS manifest log and sealed trip report for the bonded truck fleet, if required by customs
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The DGI may audit zero-rating claims retrospectively for up to five years. If the documentary bundle is incomplete, the evidence of foreign payment or physical export is missing, or the exporter does not receive and repatriate the proceeds within the governing commercial term (benchmark 180 days), the DGI will recharacterize the transaction as a taxable domestic supply. The full 7% ITBMS becomes due, plus late surcharges and default interest from the original invoice date. Fines range from 50% to 100% of the omitted tax, and fraudulent documentation or false customs declarations constitute tax evasion, carrying criminal penalties of up to five years’ imprisonment, disqualification of the taxpayer, and loss of eligibility for future export zero-rating and bonded-cargo licenses.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Superintendencia de Bancos de Panamá (SBP); Banco Nacional de Panamá (state-owned fiscal agent and clearing hub); monetary and exchange policy administered by the Ministry of Economy and Finance (MEF). There is no issuing central bank; the U.S. Dollar is full legal tender.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Panama operates a fully dollarized, exchange-control-free regime. Both current and capital account transactions are freely convertible; no central bank approval is required for profit remittances, dividends, loan repayments, or inbound capital. The Panamanian balboa (PAB) is a subdivision coinage unit pegged 1:1 to the USD. Practical compliance friction is limited to SBP AML reporting of cash transactions above USD 10,000 and DGI tax-filing obligations, not to convertibility restrictions.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: None. Statutory retention is 100% of export and eligible service receipts; no mandatory surrender timeline, no conversion ratio, and no repatriation window applies to bonded trucking revenues. Exporters and service providers must, however, preserve settlement evidence, bills of lading, and airway bills for at least five years for SBP and DGI audit purposes.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Treasury clearing and reserve account (USD); capital escrow account
Operational corporate account (USD) with SWIFT MT103/MT101 clearing and online treasury
Commercial operating and payroll account (USD); trade finance account
Trade settlement and documentary letter of credit account (USD)
Merchant clearing and ACH disbursement account (USD)
Contingency liquidity and secondary clearing account (USD)

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Medium-Low. Panama does not maintain a dedicated EMI license class. Offshore digital banks and EMIs (Wise, Airwallex, Mercury, Payoneer, Currencycloud) generally decline Panamanian Private Interest Foundations due to enhanced due diligence exposure, or require an SBP-licensed local branch or sponsor bank. Local fintechs operate under SBP payment aggregator or savings-and-credit licenses and lack the clearing capability for a bonded airport feeder fleet. A fintech overlay may serve as a supplementary disbursement rail only, never as the primary treasury anchor.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Physical attendance is effectively mandatory for at least one signatory director or officer and the foundation's registered agent during initial onboarding at tier-1 institutions. Remote video onboarding is accepted only as a secondary channel when an existing SBP-licensed relationship or an institutional referral exists. A fully digital remote opening for a PIF without any in-person interview is not a viable compliance path.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Private Interest Foundation opacity, bearer participation certificates, or nominee council structure under Law 25 of 1995
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certified copy of the foundation charter (Escritura Pública) recorded at the Public Registry; current Registered Agent certificate; formal Beneficial Owner declaration compliant with Law 23 of 2015; unconditional confidentiality waiver addressed to SBP; written confirmation that no bearer participation certificates are outstanding.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Lack of economic substance and insufficient nexus with Panama in the ISIC 5222 bonded truck fleet activity
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Lease or title evidence for the fleet yard and administrative office in Panama; payroll records or service contracts for Panamanian drivers and mechanics; GPS-monitoring agreement with a licensed tracking provider; Tocumen International Airport access and handling permits; vehicle registration certificates with Panamanian plates and local insurance policies.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Unclear source of funds for the foundation's mandatory capital endowment and fleet pre-paid expenses
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Source-of-funds letter executed by the founder and each contributing council member; audited financial statements or certified bank reference letter of the contributor; SWIFT or correspondent wire evidence; board resolution approving the capital endowment plan and itemized budget for truck purchase, fuel, tolls, and airport concession fees.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-volume cross-border wire activity to freight forwarders and third-party road transporters outside Panama
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Executed master service agreements and commercial invoices between the PIF and each overseas counterparty; airport cargo manifests and consolidated airway bills; GPS route logs demonstrating actual bonded carriage; customs processing receipts from legal authorities; full corporate KYC pack for each non-resident forwarder.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Tax-haven profiling or OFAC/UN sanctions screening mismatch in the ultimate beneficial ownership chain
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Registered asset register proving physical truck fleet investment in Panama; clean sanctions and PEP screening report produced under SBP Rule 02-2021; undertaking to maintain books and records in Panama; commitment to file annual audited financial statements with SBP and DGI; certification that neither the foundation nor final beneficiaries appear on OFAC, EU, or UN sanctions lists.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound founding capital is wired from abroad via Fedwire or CHIPS to a U.S. correspondent bank of the Panamanian institution, then credited domestically through RTGS/ACH to the PIF's Banistmo or Banco National operating account. The SWIFT MT103 free-text and purpose code must state: 'Capital contribution to a Private Interest Foundation constituted under Law 25 of 1995; funding for GPS-sealed bonded truck fleet engaged in airport feeder service (ISIC 5222)'. Verification protocol requires notarized council minutes, a capital allocation schedule by individual truck unit or equipment line, and a Beneficial Owner declaration. The statutory minimum endowment of USD 10,000 (or the equivalent in permitted assets) must be evidenced in escrow within one year of constitution.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Clearing rails are split by geography and counterparty type: (i) domestic fuel, tolls, driver wages, and airport concession payments are settled via ACH Panama and local RTGS in USD; (ii) cross-border payments to non-resident forwarders and equipment suppliers are executed through SWIFT MT103/M10 over the correspondent banking network of the selected tier-1 institution; (iii) high-value trailer and bonded-cargo handling equipment is settled under commercial letters of credit (MT700) or documentary collections, with necessary cargo manifests, GPS route evidence, and customs receipt bundles attached. All transactions remain USD-denominated; no cross-currency conversion is required inside Panama.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Onshore deliverable FX forwards (EUR/USD, USD/MXN, USD/CRC, USD/COP) contracted with SBP-licensed banks
Offshore non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) for Latin-American currencies (COP, CLP, GTQ, CRC, PAB-nominated synthetic) arranged through regulated international counterparties
Cross-currency swaps (EUR/USD, USD/MXN) used to hedge trailer equipment financing and long-term vehicle leases
FX collars and average-rate forwards overlay for regional fuel and toll expenditure in USD
Foreign currency options (EUR/USD) under SBP-sanctioned derivatives documentation with a licensed Panama bank

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: PIF Annual Government Fee (Impuesto Anual de Fundacion de Interes Privado); official payment receipt stamped by DGI and retained by the Registered Agent
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Direccion General de Ingresos (DGI), Ministry of Economy and Finance (MEF); payable at Banco Nacional de Panama, Caja de Ahorros, or DGI e-Tax portal
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually no later than June 30 of the calendar year; payment window opens January 1; assessed on the foundation capital tier in force on January 1 (standard tier for capital up to USD 10,000 = USD 350; USD 10,001-100,000 = USD 500; USD 100,001-1,000,000 = USD 750; over USD 1,000,000 = USD 1,000)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-paid ounces between July 1 and December 31 incur a USD 50.00 surcharge; after December 31, monthly interest and recargos accrue under the Fiscal Code; the foundation cannot obtain a DGI Paz y Salvo tax clearance or Registry certificate; two or more consecutive unpaid years trigger DGI delinquency certification and administrative strike-off (cancellation) by the Registro Publico.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Corporate Income Tax Return (Declaracion Jurada Anual de Impuesto sobre la Renta, Form 1075 for legal entities) covering Panama-source income from bonded road feeder trucking services
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Direccion General de Ingresos (DGI) via the GDI e-Tax / virtual office system
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually by March 15 immediately following the December 31 fiscal year-end; any alternative fiscal year requires prior DGI authorization
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Monthly surcharges of 5% on the tax due, capped at 50% for prolonged non-filing; late-filing fines of USD 100.00 to USD 1,000.00; criminal tax evasion liability if concealment is proven; blocking of Paz y Salvo issuance, which in turn blocks ATTT and ANA renewals.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Beneficial Owner Confirmation Filing (Confirmacion Anual de Informacion del Beneficiario Final in the Registro de Transparencia y Beneficiario Final via the SBF electronic module)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Direccion General de Ingresos (DGI) - Sistema de Beneficiario Final (SBF)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually by March 31 for information current as of December 31 of the preceding year; interim updates (council member changes, protector appointment, beneficiary substitutions) must be filed within 15 business days
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Fines of USD 100.00 to USD 1,000.00 per omission or inaccuracy per reporting period under Law 70 of 2019 and Regulatory Decree 244 of 2019; suspension of Registro Publico services and denial of Paz y Salvo; repeated non-compliance is grounds for administrative cancellation.

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 25% (general/normal rate; progressive statutory rates also apply: 10% on the first USD 50,000 of net taxable income; 15% on net taxable income from USD 50,001 to USD 1,500,000; the 25% rate applies to net taxable income above USD 1,500,000 per Law 8 of 2010 / Fiscal Code, as amended)
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Territorial tax system: foreign-source income is fully exempt from ISR. PIF vehicles: flat annual state tax of USD 350 (Law 25 of 1995) is the only levy for offshore/economically inert foundations; no withholding or corporate tax on distributions of foreign income to non-resident beneficiaries. No general Panamanian tax holidays apply to the bonded airport-feeder trucking business (ISIC 5222); specific regimes (Panama Pacífico 0% ISR; SEM headquarters; Duty-free/City of Knowledge) are inapplicable to a customs bonded road transport operation. The bonded trucking activity earns Panama-source income and therefore cannot rely on the territorial exemption.
